title: CommitLoreBench run record
description: One line of bench/results/*.jsonl. One line = one (task, condition, seed) run.

run_id.description: Identifies the runner invocation. Every row of one invocation shares it.

harness_commit.description: Commit resolved from git HEAD once when the benchmark matrix started.

dist_digest.description: SHA-256 of every path and file in dist/, resolved once when the benchmark matrix started.

cond.description: Condition arm. commitlore-on and commitlore-off are the two arms of the primary comparison; no-scope, no-grade and no-lifecycle are the T-703 ablation arms, each the treatment minus one guarantee. Deliberately NOT an enum: bench/types.ts registers conditions as an open string set so an arm can be added without a schema change, and closing it here would reject rows from a run whose arm is already registered (records-uninjected is the next one). The arms that exist are listed in `examples` and in bench/README.md; a typo'd arm is caught by the runner at parse time, which is where it can still be fixed for free.

seed.description: Seed fixing the workspace commit dates and the dry-run driver's PRNG.

reproposed.description: detect.reproposed_if matched the agent's transcript, diff or commits.

violations.description: Number of detect.violation_if clauses that matched.

stopped_by.description: How the run ended, distinguishing an enforced stop from an observed overrun. completed=finished within every budget. timeout=wall clock elapsed and the harness killed the process. over-turns=finished on its own having exceeded the turn budget (the claude CLI has no --max-turns, so the budget is observed, not applied). over-tokens=global token cap exhausted; with turns=0 and tokens=0 the run never started. error=driver or setup failure, so the row carries no usable measurement.

model.description: The agent model that produced the run, e.g. claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. Re-proposal behaviour is model-dependent, so every rate derived from these rows is conditional on this value. New runner rows always emit it (dry-run uses "dry-run"; a non-simulated run requires --model). It remains optional in the schema only so older JSONL artifacts validate and metrics can report their model as "(unrecorded)" rather than silently averaging across unknown models.

guard_exposure.description: Guard-hook observations from this run. Optional only for legacy rows created before exposure instrumentation; missing means unknown, never no exposure.

complete.description: Whether the guard could complete its history and notes scan. False is unknown exposure, never a no-fire result.

executed.description: Whether the guard hook actually ran at least once.

checks.description: Edit proposals checked by the guard.

fires.description: Checks that matched a ruled-out alternative.

matches.description: Matched alternatives and the edit path, retained for audit without re-running the agent. A null alternative identifies a blocked record whose content was withheld.

simulated.description: True when the driver fabricated the transcript. Simulated rows are never evidence.

matched.description: Labels of the detector clauses that fired, for auditing a judgement.

error.description: Failure detail, or why a run was skipped.

harvest_tokens.description: CPAA numerator, first term: model tokens the harvest step spent drafting records for this run. Optional — the harness records it only when a harvest actually ran, because a fabricated 0 would price CommitLore's record-writing pipeline as free.

verify_tokens.description: CPAA numerator, second term: model tokens the verification step spent checking those drafts. Structurally 0 for the shipped verifier (src/core/harvest-verify.ts is deterministic and calls no model), but a measured 0 is a different claim from an absent field, so it is written only when the step ran.

accepted_records.description: CPAA denominator: records present in the repository this run started from, counted after seeding and before the agent ran. The control arm strips the trailer block, so it reports 0 — which is why metrics.ts reports CPAA as undefined rather than dividing by it. metrics.ts uses a row only when it carries all three of harvest_tokens, verify_tokens and accepted_records; a denominator with no numerator would price accepted records at zero.
